newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal revises 1997 GDP forecast upwards - papers.
newsitem.headline: Portugal revises 1997 GDP forecast upwards - papers.

text.p: The Portuguese government has revised upwards its forecast for economic growth in 1997 to 3.3 percent from the three percent it was expecting previously, newspapers reported on Friday.
The revised growth forecast was implicit in the economic projections for 1998-2000 which were being sent to parliament and the European Commission on Friday, they said.
The economy is officially expected to have grown by up to three percent in 1996 although no final figure has yet been published.
According to the 1998-2000 'Convergence Programme', the state deficit will fall to 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2000 from the forecast 2.9 percent this year.
The limit for entry into the European Union's economic and monetary union (EMU) is three percent.
Portugal's inflation rate at the start of the next millenium should be around 1.8 percent, down from the projected 2.5 percent for 1997. Inflation is projected to slow to 2.3 percent in 1998.
The figures were carried by the Diario de Noticias, Publico and Diario Economico citing ministerial sources.
The debt-to-GDP ratio, also one of the EMU entry tests, is seen falling inside the Maastricht Treaty target in 2000 when it should reach 59.5 percent.

The EMU blueprint calls for a debt ratio of 60 percent although it is also important that the figure be on a downward path. For 1998, the government forecast a debt ratio of 62.5 percent, down from an expected 64.3 percent in 1997.
